objective: Put the overlay in the zip a player downloads, prove it is there, and stop the tester docs from lying. scripts/package_mvp_windows.ps1 stages server, assumptions, engine, web and packaging and no overlay; packaging/README.txt tells players the hotkey overlay 'ships in a later build' and describes the overlay in the future tense. This stage adds an -OverlayDir parameter that stages TASK-215-S1's packaged app to <stage>/overlay/ (the exact path packaging/launch.py resolves in TASK-215-S2), an explicit OVERLAY STUB when it is omitted — mirroring the existing engine-runtime stub so a stub build fails honestly instead of mysteriously — a clean-room assertion that the extracted zip really contains the executable, and a README rewrite in the present tense. Runs AFTER S1 and S2 are on main: it depends on S1's artifact name and S2's resolved path.
constraints: The staged layout is fixed by TASK-215-S2: <stage>/overlay/PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay.exe plus the rest of the packaged app folder alongside it. -OverlayDir points at TASK-215-S1's output directory (overlay/dist-win/PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay-win32-x64) and MUST be validated the way -RuntimeDir is: if the executable is not in it, throw with a message naming the missing path.

Without -OverlayDir, stage <stage>/overlay/OVERLAY-STUB.txt — same posture as the existing engine runtime stub. The launcher's honest 'no overlay in this build' line (TASK-215-S2, AC-4) is then what a player sees. Never stage a half-overlay and never silently omit the directory.

packaging/README.txt must stop describing the overlay in the future tense. Delete both 'later build' claims and rewrite the PRIVACY paragraph's 'The upcoming overlay will read...' into present tense. State: the overlay starts automatically with run.bat, the default hotkey is Ctrl+Alt+D (OVERLAY_HOTKEY overrides), showing it never steals game focus, 'open details' opens the browser, and run.bat --no-overlay runs the web page alone. In a stub build the README must not claim the overlay is present.

packaging/test_launch.py already asserts what the Windows package script stages (test_package_script_stages_all_launchers / test_package_script_stages_real_engine). Extend that Linux-runnable pattern: the required check must fail today and pass after this stage, by parsing the .ps1 for the overlay staging and the stub branch. That text-level assertion is the only mechanical gate available off Windows and it is required, not optional.

Do not weaken the clean-room script. Add overlay assertions in BOTH modes (real overlay staged -> executable present in the extracted zip; -ExpectStubRuntime style stub mode -> OVERLAY-STUB.txt present and no executable). Note issue #134 (flaky 'port still bound after stop'): do not attempt to fix it here and do not relax any existing assertion to route around it.
Do not launch the overlay from the clean-room script's assertions — the runner is headless and Electron would hang. Assert the artifact's presence and the launcher's log line, not a running window.
Existing tests may be EXTENDED, never deleted or skipped.
Branch backend/TASK-215-S3-<slug>. A literal role/... branch is refused by completion proof #4.

Issue #145 is the PARENT of three stages and S3 is the LAST one: this is the only TASK-215 PR that may use a closing keyword on #145, and it belongs in the PR body only. Observed 2026-08-04 twice: PR #147 (S2) closed the parent while S1 and S3 were unstarted, and PR #148 re-closed it from a commit message that only quoted the keyword — GitHub parses commit messages that reach main too. Until this stage is genuinely the last one landing, write 'Refs #145'. Do not open S3 before S1's artifact contract is on main.
forbidden_actions: Editing packaging/launch.py, packaging/run.bat, anything under overlay/, or anything under .github/
Removing or loosening any existing assertion in scripts/cleanroom_windows_check.ps1
Shipping an overlay directory that is neither a validated packaged app nor an explicit stub
Claiming in README.txt that the overlay ships when the zip was packaged without -OverlayDir

acceptance_criteria.text: scripts/package_mvp_windows.ps1 accepts -OverlayDir, validates that it contains PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay.exe (throwing a message that names the missing path otherwise), and stages the whole packaged app folder to <stage>/overlay/ preserving PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay.exe at <stage>/overlay/PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay.exe.

Without -OverlayDir the script stages <stage>/overlay/OVERLAY-STUB.txt explaining what belongs there, how to repackage with -OverlayDir, and that the launcher will report no overlay — and it prints a summary NOTE at the end, exactly as the runtime stub does.

packaging/test_launch.py gains an assertion that the Windows package script stages the overlay directory in both modes (real and stub) at the exact path packaging/launch.py resolves; the test fails against main's script and passes after this change.

scripts/cleanroom_windows_check.ps1 asserts, on the EXTRACTED zip, that overlay/PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay.exe exists in a real build and that OVERLAY-STUB.txt (and no executable) exists in a stub build. No existing assertion is removed or loosened.

packaging/README.txt contains no 'later build' claim and no future-tense overlay description; grep for 'later build' and 'upcoming overlay' over packaging/README.txt returns nothing (asserted by a test).

packaging/README.txt tells a player, in the RUN and FIRST VERDICT sections: the overlay starts automatically with run.bat, the default hotkey is Ctrl+Alt+D and OVERLAY_HOTKEY overrides it, the card never steals game focus, 'open details' opens the browser page, and run.bat --no-overlay runs the web page alone.

The PRIVACY/SAFETY section states the shipped posture in present tense and unchanged in substance: clipboard text the game produces on Ctrl+C and Client.txt only, no memory reads, no injection, no input automation, one action per keypress, localhost only (S1/S2/S3 of the doctrine).
Both required checks pass; no test deleted or skipped; packaging/launch.py, packaging/run.bat and everything under overlay/ are byte-identical to main.

rollback: Revert the branch; the zip returns to its current overlay-free contents and the README to its current (dishonest) future tense — so this rollback is only correct alongside reverting the mission claim.
